speaker: Doctor
text: Let's start by clarifying your symptoms: when does the shooting ear pain occur, and does it happen even when you aren't wearing earrings?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: That shooting pain while eating is very concerning for Frey's syndrome, but could it also be related to the recent surgery or an infection? REQUEST TEST: Audiogram and Tympanometry. Did you notice any drainage or hearing changes specifically when you eat?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand your concern, but I must evaluate the clinical picture thoroughly before confirming a diagnosis. Has the pain ever radiated to your cheek or jaw when eating, and do you notice any redness or warmth over the earlobe?

REQUEST TEST: Autonomic response monitoring; DIAGNOSIS READY: Frey's Syndrome (Gustatory Sweating).
